title: Job scope, ownership and safe authorisation
audience: Trainees and new workers on the roof soft washing track, and supervisors who decide whether a roof job may be scheduled. Completing this lesson does not grant any roof-work or height authority.
learningOutcomes: Identify who owns and controls the roof, any solar equipment and any shared or strata property affected by the job.
Separate the decisions a worker may observe and record from those reserved to qualified roof, electrical, chemical or environmental specialists.
Apply a hold, restricted-scope or stop-work decision to a paper-based job pack in which authority or evidence is missing.
referencesAtStart: Official sources for this lesson: SafeWork NSW, Work safely at heights in construction (no date shown); Safe Work Australia, Model Code of Practice: Managing the risk of falls at workplaces (no date shown); SafeWork NSW, Work on roofs: commercial and industrial buildings (code of practice) (cover dated May 2026; commencement 22 May 2026); SafeWork SA, High-risk construction work changes for PCBUs and principal contractors (March 2026).

instruction.heading: Why ownership and authority come first
instruction.body: A roof soft washing job starts with the question of who may let the work happen. The owner of the building, the body corporate or strata manager for common property, the owner of any solar array, and the occupant may each hold a different part of the decision. A request from one occupant does not establish authority over the whole roof, the skylights, the gutters or the equipment mounted on it. Record the name, role and approval date of each person whose consent is needed, and do not schedule roof access until those approvals exist.

instruction.heading: Scope the job in writing
instruction.body: Write down what is included: which roof planes, gutters, roof edges and related surfaces, the method and the products, and the times. Write down what is excluded: roof repairs, re-sheeting, roof integrity assessment, solar panel cleaning under a separate scope, and high-pressure roof jetting. A soft washing job scope that does not state its exclusions invites a dispute about what was promised. Mark every part of the roof that cannot be seen from the ground as an unknown.

instruction.heading: Ground-based alternatives and the height hierarchy
instruction.body: Apply the height hierarchy before any roof access is considered. SafeWork NSW's construction guidance (no date shown) puts the options in order: first, ground-level or existing solid-structure working where that is possible; second, fall-prevention devices such as work platforms, roof-edge barriers or scaffolding; third, work-positioning systems; and fall-arrest systems last. For fragile surfaces, the same guidance points to covers over skylights, crawl boards and exclusion zones marked out in the work area. Ask whether any part of the job can be done from the ground with a method that does not need roof access, and record the answer.

instruction.heading: Recognise what the worker may and may not decide
instruction.body: A worker may observe the roof from a safe position, record visible conditions, photograph them, and report them. A worker may not decide that a roof is structurally sound, that a material is not fragile, that a chemical is compliant, or that a runoff rule is met. Those decisions belong to a competent person, the relevant specialist or the site controller. Keep the observed facts separate from the unverified statements in every record.

instruction.heading: Regulatory context for roof cleaning
instruction.body: Safe Work Australia's model code on managing the risk of falls (no date shown) says to check with the regulator whether it has legal effect in the jurisdiction; that it has legal effect only where a jurisdiction adopts it is not confirmed by an official source. The NSW code for work on roofs of commercial and industrial buildings took effect on 22 May 2026 (cover dated May 2026) and excludes residential roofs. It lists roof-material cleaning among the work it covers, but its text does not mention gutter cleaning or soft washing, so the NSW position for soft washing is only partly confirmed. Work over 2 metres needs fall-prevention controls; whether the high-risk work rules apply at 2 metres is not confirmed by an official source. SafeWork NSW's construction guidance requires a safe work method statement (SWMS) for work where a person could fall more than 2 metres. In South Australia, from 1 July 2026, construction work that involves a risk of falling more than two metres is high-risk construction work, and SafeWork SA's March 2026 guidance (no day shown) says a SWMS must be prepared before the work starts. Check the rule for the state where the job sits.

instruction.heading: Stop-work and hold decisions
instruction.body: Issue a hold notice when authority, a roof assessment, access planning or a competent person's confirmation is missing. Stop work when the roof is fragile or unknown, the weather changes, a skylight or opening is unprotected, a person or animal enters the exclusion zone, or a solar array or electrical service is found where the scope did not say it would be. A customer's wish to finish the job is not a reason to continue past any of these conditions.

instruction.heading: Licence and authority boundary
instruction.body: Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, roof-work authority or height authority. No licence for roof soft washing as such is confirmed. Obtain the employer's written authorisation, and check the state rule, before any roof access.

procedure: Identify the owner, the body corporate or strata manager, any solar array owner and the occupant, and record each person whose approval is needed.
Write the scope, including the roof areas, gutters, method, products and times, and state the exclusions.
Mark every roof area that cannot be seen from the ground as an unknown.
Apply the height hierarchy and record whether any part of the job can be done from the ground.
Confirm the applicable state rule and record any gap for follow-up.
Check the stop-work conditions and record any that apply.
Issue a hold notice if authority, a roof assessment or access planning is missing, and name the person who must resolve it.
Record the decision, the people told and the approvals still outstanding before the job is rescheduled.

workedExamples.situation: A property owner asks for a roof wash tomorrow. They have not shown a roof assessment, and they are unsure who owns the solar panels on the roof.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What is the first safe action, and who must be told?
workedExamples.reasoning: Issue a hold notice. Roof access cannot be planned until the ownership of the solar equipment and the owner's authority are confirmed, and until a competent person has assessed the roof. Tell the owner in writing which approvals are missing, and ask for the solar owner's details. Record the request, the date, the people contacted and the unknowns. Do not attend the roof.

workedExamples.situation: A strata manager agrees to a soft wash of the roof of a block of units, but the common-property roof has skylights, and the scope does not mention them.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: What must the scope record before work starts?
workedExamples.reasoning: The skylights are an unknown risk that the scope has not addressed. Record them as a fragile-surface hazard, require skylight protection or exclusion as the hierarchy calls for, and have the scope updated and approved. Work does not start until the scope, the protection and the approval are recorded.

equipmentAndPpe: Job pack with ownership record, scope and exclusions
Roof sketch or photographs marked with fragile areas, skylights and exclusion zones
Hold notice template and job record with verified and unknown columns
PPE as specified in the job pack for the site

commonErrors.error: Accepting one occupant's request as approval for work on common property or a solar array.
commonErrors.prevention: Record the approval of each person whose consent is needed before scheduling access.

commonErrors.error: Leaving the exclusions out of the scope.
commonErrors.prevention: Write the exclusions in the scope and have them approved.

commonErrors.error: Recording a roof as sound or non-fragile from the ground.
commonErrors.prevention: Record it as unknown until a competent person has assessed it.

commonErrors.error: Assuming a residential or commercial code applies without checking.
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state rule and record any gap for follow-up.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: The NSW construction guidance orders the options: ground-level or existing solid-structure working first, then fall-prevention devices, then work-positioning, with fall arrest last (page dated no date shown).

Model code: Safe Work Australia's model falls code says to check with the regulator whether it has legal effect in the jurisdiction; that it has legal effect only where a jurisdiction adopts it is not confirmed by an official source.

NSW code for work on roofs of commercial and industrial buildings took effect 22 May 2026 (cover dated May 2026). It excludes residential roofs and does not mention gutter cleaning or soft washing (only partly confirmed).
Licence notice: This lesson does not grant a licence, certificate, roof-work or height authority.

qualityStandard: Every person whose approval is needed is named, and the approval is recorded before roof access is scheduled.
The scope lists the included areas, the method and the exclusions.
Every roof area not seen from the ground is recorded as an unknown.
Each absent approval leads to a logged pause, reduced-scope or halt ruling.
documentationEvidence: Ownership and approval record for the roof, any solar array and any common property
Written scope with included and excluded items
Verified observations and unknowns recorded separately
Hold, stop-work or referral record with the person notified and the approval still outstanding
summary: Roof access needs approval from each person who controls the roof, the common property or any solar equipment.
Apply the height hierarchy and check whether a ground-based method can meet the scope.
A worker records what is seen, and specialists decide what is structurally sound, fragile or compliant.
This lesson grants no roof-work, height or licence authority.

knowledgeChecks.question: A single occupant asks for a roof wash. Which approval is also needed before roof access is scheduled?
options: Only the occupant's own signature on the access form, the booking, the job sheet and the invoice
A weather forecast for the day of the wash, the week and the whole month ahead
A quote from another business for the same roof and the same work on the site
The approval of each person who controls the roof, common property or any solar equipment

knowledgeChecks.question: Which item belongs in the exclusions section of a soft wash scope?
options: Roof repairs and re-sheeting
The method and products
The times the job will run
The customer's contact number

knowledgeChecks.question: Under the height hierarchy, what should be considered first for a roof job?
options: Fall-arrest systems on the roof edge
Whether any part can be done from the ground
Work-positioning systems for the roof plane
Roof access by ladder to the ridge line and beyond

knowledgeChecks.question: Which decision is reserved to a competent person or specialist, not the worker?
options: Recording that a gutter is visibly full of leaves
Photographing a visible crack in a skylight for the file
Deciding that the roof is structurally sound and not fragile
Reporting a missing edge barrier to the site contact on the day

knowledgeChecks.question: What does the NSW SafeWork code for work on roofs (commenced 22 May 2026) say about its scope?
options: It covers all roofs, including residential ones, with no exclusions at all
Whether it is a licence for soft washing of roofs and gutters in the state is not confirmed by an official source
It has no connection to roof cleaning or to gutters and the work at all
It states that it is not intended to apply to work on residential roofs
